newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Highlands to review Porgera offer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Highlands to review Porgera offer.

text.p: The board of Highlands Gold Ltd will be reviewing over the Christmas period an offer by Placer Dome Inc to cancel its interest in Highlands for a 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine in Papua New Guinea, Highland's managing director, Ian Goddard said on Monday.
"The board will have look at that very carefully over the next few days," Goddard told Reuters by telephone from Brisbane.
Goddard said the offer, made earlier on Monday, would take time to fully evaluate.
"I don't think the board would be able to meet and thoroughly consider it and get out a reponse before Christmas, but certainly we'll be meeting and talking," he said.

Highlands said earlier on Monday that its directors had unanimously resolved to reject a takeover bid by Placer Dome, citing an independent report by Barings Bros Burrows showing Highlands shares to be worth about 40 percent more than Placer's 75 cent per share offer price.
Placer Dome has about 33 percent of the PNG miner.
Both companies have 25 percent stakes in Porgera, Placer's being held through its listed Placer Pacific Ltd unit.
The other equal 25 percent shareholders in Porgera are Goldfields Ltd and PNG interests.
The PNG interests are held 15 percent by Orogen Minerals Ltd and 10 percent by the government's Minerals Development Resources Corp (MRDC).
The MRDC holds five percent in its own right and five percent for provincial governments and landowners.
Production from the mine should total about 850,000 ounces of gold this year, Goddard said.

Analysts said the latest offer by Placer Dome made more sense for the Canadian company, given its prime interest in Porgera to the exclusion of Highland's prospective Frieda-Nena copper and gold deposit and its Ramu nickel-cobalt find.
Highland shares closed two cents higher at A$0.77.
